summary.headline: Marksans Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.6% YoY to INR841 crore, with record EBITDA of INR213 crore (25.3% margin) and PAT of INR159 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR840.8 crore grew 35.6% YoY, led by UK and Europe at INR356 crore (+74.7%), which includes INR44 crore from the QliniQ acquisition. Gross margin expanded to 59.1% on product mix, low-cost inventory and favourable FX, and EBITDA margin reached 25.3%. Management said the gross margin is sustainable at around 55-56% as freight and raw material costs from the war normalise, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin. Cash rose to INR1,058 crore, with net cash of INR1,031 crore after the QliniQ payment.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue INR377 crore, +15.1% YoY, about 45% of consolidated revenue. Summer demand softer in line with seasonality; Rx price erosion remained in single digits; Canada filings underway.

segments.name: UK and Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR356 crore, +74.7% YoY, about 42% of revenue and a record quarter. Ex-QliniQ growth was over 50% YoY, all organic in the UK. QliniQ (Netherlands) contributed INR44 crore; growth ex-QliniQ was 53.1%.

segments.name: Australia and New Zealand
segments.commentary: Revenue INR88 crore, +53.7% YoY; sequential moderation was seasonal after a strong Q4 Southern Hemisphere winter.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR20 crore. Management said Middle East and other non-western markets are being hit by shipping disruption from the war.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 20-21%; management said it will stick with this given geopolitical volatility.
Gross margin sustainable at roughly 55-56%, versus 59% in Q1, as inventory benefit fades and freight and raw material costs stay elevated.
Europe revenue expected at about INR180 crore for FY27. QliniQ guided to INR150-175 crore for the year, with its EUR10 million base growing to EUR14-15 million.
Q2 revenue expected to be above Q1 and Q3 the strongest; EBITDA margin to reach the guided level. Year-end EBITDA margin of 21-22% described as achievable.
Target of INR4,000 crore revenue within two years reiterated; US target moves from $200 million to $300 million, then $400 million over about five years.
Germany expected to generate revenue from early Q3 FY27; Ireland revenue not expected until FY28. Europe target of about INR1,000 crore within five years.
capex_capacity: Goa Unit 2 (Teva facility) revenue at INR50-plus crore against an INR80 crore target, about 60-65% of plan.
Management is evaluating one or two targets for a new Indian manufacturing unit over one to two years; nothing concrete yet. Location open, including other states.
Backward integration (DMFs, CRAMS) is not being actively pursued given the current environment.
Around 65-70% of sales are manufactured in India.
Net capex was INR33 crore in Q1.
demand_pricing: US order book described as strong. US growth expected from all subsidiaries this year, not only the US.
US Rx mix is rising; the US business is still OTC-led, possibly moving from 95:5 OTC:Rx toward 85:15 over time.
UK is about 55% Rx and 45% OTC; Europe is expected to be about 80-85% Rx.
Management sees no major change in US OTC competitive intensity; some large players are struggling.
Rx price erosion in the US stayed in single digits.
Inventory-led margin benefit is being depleted over time; freight and solvent costs are rising due to the war.

qa_highlights.question: How is QliniQ revenue recognised, and what is the FY27 outlook for Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective date was 1 April 2026, so Q1 is consolidated. QliniQ is guided at INR150-175 crore for FY27, and total Europe about INR180 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin sustainable at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 55-56% as the inventory benefit unwinds, and says more upside is unrealistic given freight and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan with over INR1,000 crore of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is earmarked for inorganic growth, mainly in Europe, with nothing concrete yet. Management ruled out riskier instruments such as index investing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise guidance upward?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin stands, given geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US strategy in light of tariff comments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not weight the tariff remarks heavily. US remains an important market, and local manufacturing is an option to keep open.

qa_highlights.question: Could ABCnow and QliniQ scale in the UK and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QliniQ is Rx-tilted, ABCnow has Rx and OTC, and Europe is about 80-85% Rx. Europe is targeted at about INR1,000 crore in five years, mostly through acquisitions.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalising from 59.1% to 55-56% as inventory benefit fades and war-driven freight and solvent costs persist.
Shipping and freight disruption in Rest of World and Middle East markets.
US tariff and policy uncertainty; management expects the policy to change and has not committed to US manufacturing.
Integration and returns on the QliniQ and ABCnow acquisitions; Ireland revenue timing pushed to FY28.
Capacity: management says a new India unit may be needed for the three to five year plan, but nothing is confirmed. Goa Unit 2 is running at 60-65% of plan.
No definite timeline for the next USFDA inspection across the three US-approved plants.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability but cautious on forward margins and capital deployment. Management repeatedly tied margin and guidance to geopolitical and freight risk, and was non-committal on large M&A and on US manufacturing.
